s1.syndrome_frame: Gastrointestinal syndrome with vomiting, hematemesis, and abdominal discomfort
salient_findings: Multiple rounded, echogenic neoformations at the pyloric antrum on abdominal ultrasound
Sessile, smooth-surfaced nodules in the pyloric antrum on endoscopy
key_facts: 9-month-old spayed female Ragdoll cat
Fed a raw rabbit-based raw food (BARF) diet for 3 months
Moderately dehydrated (≈7%)
Febrile (39.9°C)
Pale mucous membranes with capillary refill time ~3 s
Mild discomfort on abdominal palpation
Body condition score was 4/9 (4.2 kg)
Complete blood count, serum biochemistry, and FIV/FeLV tests were within normal limits or negative
Thoracic and abdominal radiographs were unremarkable
Abdominal ultrasound revealed multiple rounded, echogenic neoformations at the pyloric antrum
Mild mesenteric lymphadenomegaly
Cytological brushing of the gastric mucosa demonstrated mucosal cells, mixed neutrophilic and macrophagic inflammation, and occasional large, non-septate hyphae

shortlist.label: Phycomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Cytological brushing of the gastric mucosa demonstrated mucosal cells, mixed neutrophilic and macrophagic inflammation, and occasional large, non-septate hyphae

shortlist.label: Gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Vomiting, hematemesis, and abdominal discomfort, with cytological brushing showing mixed neutrophilic and macrophagic inflammation

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal foreign body
shortlist.why_kept: History of eating a raw rabbit-based diet, which could lead to ingestion of foreign material

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical signs of vomiting, hematemesis, and abdominal discomfort, with abdominal ultrasound showing mild mesenteric lymphadenomegaly

shortlist.label: Gastric carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal ultrasound revealed multiple rounded, echogenic neoformations at the pyloric antrum, which could be indicative of a neoplastic process

raw.rationale: The presence of large, non-septate hyphae with irregular diameter and branching in the cytological brushing of the gastric mucosa, along with the clinical presentation of vomiting, hematemesis, and abdominal discomfort, supports the diagnosis of Phycomycosis, a fungal infection that can affect the gastrointestinal tract.

rejected.label: Gastritis
rejected.why: While gastritis could explain some of the clinical signs, it does not account for the presence of fungal hyphae.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal foreign body
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a foreign body in the abdominal radiographs or ultrasound.

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
rejected.why: The presence of fungal hyphae and the acute onset of symptoms are not typical of inflammatory bowel disease.

rejected.label: Gastric carcinoma
rejected.why: The age of the cat and the presence of fungal hyphae make gastric carcinoma less likely.
